purpose: Homecoming landing and selected pilot walking into Fury HQ

animation.background: Create a FOUR-panel production cinematic background sheet in an exactly even 2-column x 2-row grid. Each of the four panels is a WIDE 16:9 landscape shot, 840x472 pixels intended, total sheet 1680x944. Output a 16:9 four-shot sheet like INPUT 1, NOT two tall side-by-side portraits. INPUT 1 is the approved four-shot Bullets of Fury homecoming sheet; its lower two sunset HQ shots are the edit targets. INPUT 2 is the corrected empty coast and HQ architecture, which is the correct design but the wrong tall panel format. Reuse the approved wide landscape camera, sunset/coast, orange lamps, blue ocean and islands, cliffs, blue HQ globe, hangar and FURY HQ building sign. TOP LEFT: identical approved wide oblique coastal runway at sunset, remove the green aircraft completely and restore its patch of sky, empty runway. TOP RIGHT: identical approved wide FRONT view of FURY HQ at sunset and the full entire wide landing apron, with ALL SIX aircraft removed completely, exposing the unoccupied helipad, no ship shadows. Central blue-lit pedestrian/hangar entrance visible under FURY HQ sign. BOTTOM LEFT: same exact frontal TOP RIGHT camera and scenery, central HQ door opening, blue lit interior beyond. BOTTOM RIGHT: same exact frontal camera and scenery as TOP RIGHT, central HQ door fully open, warm welcome lights inside, still an empty helipad. Maintain absolutely the same environmental coordinates among the three frontal plates to animate the door without jumping. Each cell is wide 16:9, no extra headroom. No aircraft, no jets, no people, no vehicles, no baked smoke, no dialogue, no captions, no browser borders. Clean graphical detailed Neo Geo / 16-bit HD pixel art matching the approved shot. No redesign. Transparent effects are animated separately, this background is opaque. Reuse this shot. FOUR WIDE SHOTS in a 2x2 sheet.

Keep FURY HQ as part of the building sign, correct and readable, and keep the large central blue-lit entrance fully unobstructed so a pilot can walk through it. No characters, no vehicles, no small planes, no generic parked jets, no baked-in thruster trail, no aircraft. These are environment-only layers for real animated aircraft and characters. Same beautiful detailed crisp 16-bit/HD Neo Geo pixel-art style and authored lighting. Do not redesign the base; preserve this approved camera and composition. animation.cole:
Production sprite animation sheet for Bullets of Fury, using EXACT current Cole Furyship and Cole identity from the inputs. INPUT 1 current in-game green Furyship export is the strict aircraft identity reference, not a generic jet; INPUT 2 current accepted Cole full body is the strict character reference. INPUT 3 approved sunset runway/HQ is only the camera and lighting reference, never scenery in the sprites.
FRAME FORMAT: 32 frames total, exact 8 columns x 4 rows, equal 256x256 cells, total 2048x1024 intended. Genuine transparent RGBA background, no labels, no grid lines, no scenery, no text. Crisp detailed HD Neo Geo pixel art, warm sunset rim light, solid correct black costume outlines. One common scale and fixed physical pivot per animation, no movement across cells, no changing body size.
TOP TWO ROWS (16 frames, row-major 0-15): SAME green/silver current Furyship, 3/4 REAR view facing away toward Fury HQ. The fuselage is LEVEL AND HORIZONTAL with the pavement, low and shallow rear perspective, like a real aircraft on its landing wheels. Do NOT stand it upright on its tail. Nose points away and slightly right into screen, engine exhaust faces camera, landing gear bears its weight. Preserve current silhouette, pointed nose, four forward pods, twin rear engines, wing and cockpit layout. Keep the engine mounts fixed at cell(128,154), craft drawn about 180px wide, hull and wing outline same size every frame. Frame0 starts level airborne with landing gear retracted and short cyan exhaust. Frames1-5 the gear unfolds with mechanical articulation and hovering exhaust flickers. Frames6-10 gear fully extended, landing struts compress through smooth touchdown and short downwash; nose and wings remain level. Frames11-13 exhaust powers down, wheels settled, full craft looks FLAT on the ground. Frames14-15 canopy opens slightly and a narrow disembark ladder deploys on the craft's RIGHT side; ship remains stationary and grounded. No pilot aboard visible, no aircraft shadow; shadow is a separate layer. Never twist or change the aircraft. This is a landing and engine shutoff, not a flight turn or tumbling.
THIRD ROW (8 frames,16-23): ONLY Cole, the exact brown hair/beard, green military flight suit, harness, gloves and boots from body reference. Full intact person, two arms, two legs. Cole climbs down a boarding ladder toward the right side, rendered right-facing profile/3-quarter rear. No ladder included (it belongs to craft above). Animate both hands descending rungs, feet stepping down, then straightens and turns away from camera. Bottom-center foot pivot at(128,224), head height about155px, consistent proportions. Keep feet/head centered; game will move him along the ladder trajectory. His final pose looks toward HQ in 3/4 rear view.
BOTTOM ROW (8 frames,24-31): ONLY same Cole, an actual smooth repeating 8-frame walking cycle AWAY FROM THE CAMERA, slight 3/4 rear toward left, full body. One full alternating gait, heel strike, lift, opposite leg step, relaxed counter-swing arms. Camera sees back of head and green outfit, correct harness. Same bottom-center pivot(128,224), same character height155px throughout, no root movement. Frame31 loops seamlessly into frame24. Absolutely no ship in bottom two rows. This is a game-ready sheet, no contact sheet inset, no background, no invented pilot. Separate 16-frame landing +8-frame disembark +8-frame walk with all32 cells.
